description: Defines the authoritative living state of an active A.R.I.A. diagnostic case and how that state changes as context, evidence, hypotheses, probabilities, actions, findings, corrections, and validation evolve.

core_principle.statement: A diagnostic case is a versioned technical state machine, not a transcript. Conversation, documents, screenshots, measurements, actions, and historical experience contribute to the case, but the authoritative current case state shall be represented explicitly and independently of conversational order.
rules: The current case state shall represent what ARIA presently knows, suspects, has eliminated, has confirmed, has requested, and is waiting for.
Conversation history shall not serve as the authoritative case database.
Every material state change shall be attributable to an event.
Previous states shall remain reconstructable.
ARIA shall reason from current state rather than repeatedly rereading the complete case transcript.
State transitions shall preserve uncertainty.
A hypothesis is not a finding.
A corrective action is not proof of root cause.
A successful validation is not automatically proof that every causal assumption was correct.
Material state changes shall produce a new version.
Previous versions shall not be overwritten.
Nonmaterial presentation changes need not produce a diagnostic state version.
State versions shall be reproducible from the event history when practical.

reported_problem.description: Preserves the problem as originally reported separately from ARIA's normalized technical interpretation.
rules: The original problem statement shall remain available.
ARIA may normalize terminology without replacing the original report.
The reporter's proposed diagnosis shall remain distinguishable from the reported symptom.
Symptoms may exist before their cause is known.
A symptom may disappear without the root cause being proven.
Multiple symptoms may belong to one failure or multiple simultaneous failures.
Probability and hypothesis status shall remain separate.
A leading hypothesis is not a confirmed diagnosis.
Ruled-out hypotheses remain part of case history.
A ruled-out hypothesis may be reactivated only when new evidence or context justifies doing so.

finding_state.description: Confirmed findings represent technical conditions sufficiently supported by evidence.
rules: Findings shall be narrower than unsupported causal conclusions.
A finding may establish a condition without establishing why the condition exists.
Findings may become inputs to further hypotheses.
ARIA shall distinguish requesting an action from the action actually being completed.
An action shall not be treated as completed merely because instructions were provided.
Action results shall become evidence through the Evidence Engine.
Skipped and failed actions remain part of route history.
ARIA shall know exactly what the case is waiting for.
Pending items shall identify who or what is expected to satisfy them.
Satisfied pending items shall transition rather than simply disappear from history.
Material unresolved contradictions shall remain visible to reasoning.
A contradiction shall not be removed merely because one side is inconvenient to the leading hypothesis.
Corrective actions shall be distinguished from diagnostic actions.
Performing a correction does not prove the suspected cause.
The state before correction shall remain available for comparison.
Multiple simultaneous corrections shall reduce causal attribution confidence unless independently controlled.
Resolution requires explicit validation criteria.
The disappearance of one symptom may not satisfy all validation requirements.
Validation shall compare the post-correction state against applicable expected state.
Failed validation shall return the case to active reasoning from the new state rather than restart the case.
Operational resolution and causal resolution are distinct.
A case may be operationally resolved when service is restored even if exact root cause remains uncertain.
A case shall not be represented as causally resolved without sufficient evidence.
Learning eligibility shall depend on the actual resolution state.
State transitions shall be triggered by events rather than arbitrary language-model narrative.
A transition may trigger context, probability, routing, evidence, memory, or learning recalculation.
Invalid transitions shall be rejected by deterministic services.
The language model may propose a state transition but shall not silently mutate authoritative state.
State changes shall be atomic where multiple dependent updates must remain consistent.

rerouting_policy.rule: Rerouting shall begin from the newest authoritative state and shall preserve completed diagnostic work.

rules: ARIA shall not repeatedly request materially equivalent actions without justification.
If the state has not materially changed, repeating the same reasoning path shall receive a strong penalty.
A repeated action may become valid after a technical state change.
The system shall distinguish rerouting from backtracking.
Reopening shall preserve the previous resolution state.
A reopened case shall create new state versions rather than rewriting the original resolution.
Recurrence shall be visible to the Learning Engine.

case_branching.description: A case may branch when evidence indicates multiple independent technical problems.
rules: Independent failures may become child cases when separation improves reasoning clarity.
Shared evidence may remain linked to multiple cases.
Branching shall not duplicate evidence as independent observations.
Parent and child relationships shall remain explicit.

case_merge.description: Cases discovered to represent the same underlying incident may be linked or merged logically.
rules: Original case identifiers and histories shall remain preserved.
Merged cases shall not inflate learning counts.
Evidence provenance shall remain unchanged.

case_state_summary.description: Produces a compact current-state representation for working memory and model context.

example.reported_problem: Main is approximately -44 dBm and Diversity is approximately -63 dBm.
example.current_route_reason: Configuration evidence reduced configuration probability and increased the relative value of physical RF routing inspection.
example.interpretation: ARIA does not need to reread the entire conversation to continue. The current case state explicitly records where diagnosis presently stands.

engine_interfaces.context_engine: Publishes the current multidimensional technical context.
engine_interfaces.evidence_engine: Adds, validates, supersedes, contradicts, and invalidates evidence.
engine_interfaces.routing_engine: Maintains requested, completed, blocked, and candidate actions.
engine_interfaces.memory_engine: Builds working memory from current state and retrieves historical context.
engine_interfaces.learning_engine: Consumes validated completed case history after appropriate lifecycle transitions.

semantic_rules.rule: A case is an evolving technical state, not a chat transcript.
Conversation may modify case state only through attributable events.
Current state shall remain independently reconstructable from conversational wording.
Every material state change shall preserve the previous state.
Reported problems, symptoms, hypotheses, findings, diagnoses, corrections, and validation are distinct objects.
The leading hypothesis shall never be represented as confirmed solely because it has the highest probability.
Corrective action success shall not automatically prove the proposed root cause.
ARIA shall explicitly represent what the case is waiting for.
ARIA shall preserve completed work so rerouting does not become unnecessary backtracking.
Failed actions and failed validation shall become part of the new state rather than erase previous reasoning.
Operational resolution and causal resolution shall remain distinguishable.
A case may remain useful even when exact root cause is never proven.
Material contradictions shall remain active until reconciled, superseded, invalidated, or explicitly left unresolved.
Case state shall support multiple simultaneous hypotheses and multiple simultaneous failures.
A reopened case shall extend history rather than rewrite it.
Branching and merging shall preserve evidence provenance and prevent duplicate learning.
The language model may propose state changes but deterministic ARIA services shall own authoritative state transitions.
Working memory shall be generated from authoritative case state rather than treated as authoritative storage.
Case state shall preserve enough information to explain why ARIA is recommending the current next action.
ARIA shall always continue diagnosis from the newest validated state rather than blindly restart a troubleshooting sequence.
